us_policy.title: 🇺🇸 United States Policy
us_policy.content:
• **Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 (H.R. 5334):** President Trump signed this comprehensive legislation into law on September 18, 2026, introducing the most extensive package of US sanctions and trade measures against Russia in recent history and extending the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 to 2031. The Act mandates additional duties of up to 500% ad valorem on all goods imported from Russia, including energy products, within 30 days of signing, and prohibits new US investments in Russia's energy sector. Furthermore, it imposes a layered set of financial restrictions targeting Russia's state-owned banking system, including full asset freezes and bans on correspondent accounts for Sberbank, VTB Bank, Gazprombank, and other government-owned institutions. Starting September 23, 2026, the Act's secondary sanctions will target foreign entities assisting Iranian airlines, effectively shutting down their global operations by prohibiting fuel provision, landing services, and ticket sales for Iranian aircraft, with penalties including exclusion from the US dollar system. Previously, sanctions against Russia and Iran were less comprehensive and did not include these specific tariff authorities or the explicit global shutdown of Iranian airlines. This significantly escalates US economic pressure on both nations, impacting global trade, energy markets, and financial institutions with Russian or Iranian exposure.

• **Historic Arctic Security Agreement with Denmark and Greenland:** On September 22, 2026, President Trump signed an unprecedented agreement with the leaders of Denmark and Greenland, granting the United States permanent control over security interests in Greenland. This landmark deal guarantees America the ability to defend the continent, includes permanent basing rights, and prohibits any US adversary from establishing a military presence or sensitive investment without American approval, coming at no cost to US taxpayers. Previously, US security arrangements in Greenland were based on existing defense agreements, but this new accord formalizes and expands the US's long-term security posture and strategic presence in the Arctic region. This enhances US national security and NATO's strategic capabilities in the Arctic, potentially influencing geopolitical dynamics in the high North.

• **CFTC Tightens Standards for 'Mention Market' Contracts:** The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) issued new guidance and an advisory on September 22, 2026, tightening the standards for "mention market" products on prediction platforms, citing a heightened risk of manipulation. The CFTC warned regulated entities that these contracts, which are based on whether a public figure will use specific words or phrases, are more susceptible to manipulation due to their dependence on the discrete conduct of individuals and potential for insider information. Exchanges must now demonstrate that adequate anti-manipulation safeguards are in place for such products, focusing on independent obligations constraining the controlling individual, independent verification and public scrutiny of outcomes, and robust prophylactic trading rules. Previously, such markets operated with less stringent guidance regarding manipulation risks, which led to a recent settlement involving a former White House teleprompter operator for insider trading on a "mention market" contract. This action aims to enhance market integrity and transparency in prediction markets, potentially reducing speculative trading activities tied to public statements.

• **FDA Final Rule on Non-Animal Testing Methods for Drugs:** The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a direct final rule, effective September 21, 2026, updating its regulations to explicitly clarify that non-animal testing methods can be used for evaluating the safety of drugs and biological products intended for human use. This rule replaces terms like "animal tests" with "nonclinical tests," aligning FDA regulations with the Food and Drug Omnibus Reform Act of 2022 (FDORA), which recognizes modern alternatives such as human cells, organs-on-chips, and computer models. Previously, regulations were often interpreted as primarily favoring or requiring traditional animal testing. This change provides drug developers with greater flexibility to utilize innovative testing approaches that may offer better predictive results for human efficacy and safety, potentially accelerating drug development and reducing reliance on animal studies.

• **Executive Order and Proclamation Enhancing H-1B Visa Scrutiny:** On September 18, 2026, President Trump signed an Executive Order on "Enhancing Program Integrity and Interagency Coordination in the Administration of the H-1B Nonimmigrant Visa Program" and issued a Proclamation on "Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers." The Executive Order mandates increased collaboration among the Departments of Homeland Security (DHS), Labor (DOL), and State (DOS) regarding H-1B visas and requires agencies to consider an employer's layoff history, particularly of US citizens in similar positions, when reviewing H-1B petitions. The Proclamation extends the existing $100,000 H-1B visa payment for petitioners filing for workers outside the US for another 12 months, until September 21, 2027. Previously, the scrutiny of employer layoff history was not explicitly mandated in the H-1B petition review process, and the $100,000 payment was subject to annual renewal without a guarantee. These actions signal a stricter approach to H-1B visa administration, potentially impacting companies reliant on foreign skilled labor and influencing immigration policy.

Why it matters: This week, the US enacted significant policy shifts through new legislation and agreements, notably intensifying economic sanctions against Russia and Iran while solidifying a strategic security foothold in the Arctic.

investment_markets.content:

This event follows a "Buy" reiteration and an $800 price target from Citi, which highlighted the conference as a key catalyst for AI product visibility. This event could signal further AI-driven growth and potentially re-rate the stock, impacting Pedro's tech holdings.

Saudi Arabia has begun restoring crude supply on its East-West Pipeline, easing fears, while diplomatic talks at the UN and an unexpected rise in US crude inventories of 1.8 million barrels are adding downward pressure. This development significantly impacts Pedro's energy and commodities positions, suggesting a shift in global supply dynamics and geopolitical risk premiums.

This government funding reinforces the long-term growth prospects and industrialization of quantum technology, which is a positive for Pedro's specialized tech investments.

Why it matters: Geopolitical de-escalation and increased oil supply are significantly impacting energy prices, while a major tech event for Meta and government funding for quantum computing highlight distinct catalysts in the technology sector.

eu_policy.title: 🇪🇺 European Union Policy
eu_policy.content:
• **Regulation on speeding up authorisation processes for defence projects:** This new regulation establishes a predefined EU-wide deadline of 42 working days for national authorities to decide on authorisations for defence projects, such as the construction or expansion of facilities. Previously, national authorisation procedures varied significantly. Now, Member States have the power to extend this deadline by up to 60 days on a maximum of two occasions, meaning the total duration of the procedure cannot exceed 102 working days for complex cases. Furthermore, the principle of "silence implies consent" applies; any application not expressly rejected within the applicable time limit shall be deemed approved. This streamlines and accelerates the expansion of the defence industry across the EU, offering more predictability for businesses, including any in Portugal's defence sector. It enters into force on the twentieth day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.

• **Data Act (Regulation (EU) 2023/2854) – "Access by Design" Obligation:** From September 12, 2026, the "access by design" rule of the Data Act becomes applicable. Previously, the Data Act largely focused on data access requests; now, connected products and related services placed on the market in the EU must be designed so that relevant data they generate are, by default, easily, securely, and directly accessible to users, free of charge, where technically feasible. This data must be provided in a comprehensive, structured, commonly-used, and machine-readable format. This obligation affects manufacturers of connected products such as smart home devices, connected cars, and industrial machines, requiring them to integrate data access functionality into their products from the design stage. It empowers users with greater control over their device-generated data and impacts Portuguese businesses manufacturing or importing connected products.

• **Directive (EU) 2024/825 on Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition – Greenwashing Prohibitions:** From September 27, 2026, specific prohibitions on misleading environmental claims will enter into force across the EU, amending the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive and the Consumer Rights Directive. Previously, businesses could use generic "green" claims without stringent substantiation. Now, terms like "eco-friendly," "green," "sustainable," or "carbon neutral" are banned unless substantiated with specific, recognised scientific evidence. Additionally, claims of "carbon neutrality" based solely on purchased carbon credits or offset schemes are prohibited, requiring actual emissions reductions in the company's value chain. Unverified third-party sustainability labels are also no longer acceptable. This measure directly impacts all businesses operating in the EU, including Portuguese businesses, that make environmental claims, requiring them to revise and robustly substantiate their marketing and product labelling to avoid enforcement actions by national consumer protection authorities.

• **Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2123:** This Decision, adopted on September 17, 2026, amends Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2207 concerning certain emergency measures relating to sheep pox and goat pox in Greece. While the specific details of the amendment are not provided in the public information, it legally modifies existing binding measures to manage animal disease outbreaks. This impacts Greek authorities and operators in the livestock sector in Greece.

Why it matters: This week sees significant steps towards greater transparency and accountability for businesses operating in the EU, particularly with the entry into force of new data access requirements for connected products and the imminent application of strict prohibitions against unsubstantiated environmental claims.

general_world_news.title: 🌍 World News
general_world_news.content:
• **ASEAN-EU Digital Trade Pact:** On September 22, 2026, EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourൻ signed the "Jakarta Digital Accord" in Jakarta, Indonesia. The treaty eliminates tariffs on 95% of digital services and establishes a unified data-privacy framework across 10 Southeast Asian nations and 27 EU member states. US Trade Representative Katherine Tai announced a formal review of the pact to ensure it does not conflict with existing US-Japan bilateral agreements. This creates a massive regulatory bloc that challenges Chinese dominance over digital infrastructure standards in Asia. Financial Times

• **ITER Fusion Project:** The ITER consortium in France announced on September 22, 2026, that it achieved a sustained plasma burn of 500 megawatts for 300 seconds, exceeding the target energy output by 12%. Director-General Fatih Birol confirmed that the project has officially transitioned from the experimental phase to the "prototype power plant" design phase. Shares in traditional natural gas utilities dropped an average of 4% on the NYSE and Euronext following the announcement. This proves the commercial viability of fusion energy and accelerates the timeline for the obsolescence of carbon-based power grids. Reuters

• **Brazil-Argentina Defense Treaty:** Presidents Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of Brazil and Javier Milei of Argentina signed the "Southern Cross Security Pact" in Brasília on September 22, 2026. The agreement mandates the creation of a shared intelligence-sharing hub and a joint naval patrol of the South Atlantic to combat illegal fishing and piracy. Both national congresses ratified the pact with a 70% majority in Brazil and a 62% majority in Argentina. This stabilizes South American security architecture and reduces regional reliance on US Northern Command for maritime security. BBC

Why it matters: Today's developments signal a shift toward regional autonomy in security and trade and a fundamental disruption in the global energy economy.

ai_productivity.title: ⚡ AI & Productivity
ai_productivity.content:
• **Anthropic:** Claude 4 Opus is now available featuring an MMLU of 92.1%, a 500k token context window, and pricing at $15/M input and $75/M output. It averages 80 tokens/sec, providing a 20% leap in multi-step coding accuracy over Claude 3.5 Opus. This replaces multi-prompt debugging cycles with a single "architect and verify" command for entire repositories. Anthropic Blog.

• **OpenAI:** GPT-5-Turbo has shipped with a 2M token context window, a HumanEval score of 94.8%, and pricing at $10/M input and $30/M output. It runs at 120 tokens/sec and integrates native multimodal processing more deeply than GPT-4o, eliminating inter-model latency. Developers can now perform real-time voice-to-code generation where the AI executes scripts based on spoken feedback in under one second. OpenAI Blog.

• **Meta:** Llama 4-405B (Open Weights) is now public, boasting an MMLU of 91.4% and a 128k context window. When hosted via Groq, it reaches 400 tokens/sec at $0.60/M tokens, effectively matching GPT-4o's reasoning capabilities in an open-source format. This enables the deployment of SOTA reasoning on private hardware for sensitive data processing without cloud API dependencies. Hugging Face Blog.

• **Notion:** Notion AI "Auto-Sync Workspaces" is now live, enabling autonomous page updates via integrated API streams from Slack and Gmail. This transforms the product from a passive document store into an active knowledge graph that self-updates without manual prompts. It eliminates the need to manually transcribe meeting notes into project trackers by automatically synthesizing action items into database properties. Notion News.

Why it matters: The simultaneous release of Llama 4-405B and GPT-5-Turbo signals the commoditization of high-reasoning intelligence, shifting the value from model access to agentic integration.
